title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Assessing the Safety of Virtual Ward Discharge for Patients Awaiting Cardiac Surgery After Myocardial Infarction
official: A Randomized Controlled Trial Assessing the Safety of Virtual Ward Discharge for Patients Awaiting Cardiac Surgery After Myocardial Infarction
summary:
Patients who need inpatient cardiac surgery after heart attack can wait up to three weeks. During this time the majority of patients are stable but confined to a ward. Movement and social interaction is restricted.Furthermore the risk of hospital acquire infection increases and it is costly. The virtual ward offers a mechanism to keep inpatients at home. They are contacted regularly by the nursing staff and if there is a clinical issue it is escalated to the relevant team. This trial aims to randomise patients who are waiting to the virtual ward or standard care. The virtual ward patients will be brought back into hospital for surgery the night before or the day of the operation. This pilot study aims to assess the safety of this strategy

In clinically stable patients awaiting CABG following AMI, management via virtual wards will result in comparable clinical safety outcomes to traditional inpatient care, while improving resource utilization.

interventions.name: Discharged to a virtual ward with remote monitoring and clinical oversight while awaiting urgent cardiac surgery

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Have undergone at least three days of inpatient hospitalization.
2. Be deemed suitable for virtual ward management following a consensus agreement by the multidisciplinary team (MDT), including cardiologists and surgeons. They can be included if they are pending further investigations.
3. Be adults aged 18 years or older.
4. Have been accepted for urgent, but not emergency, cardiac surgery.
5. Be hemodynamically stable at the time of assessment.
6. Exhibit no ongoing ischemia or intractable symptoms.
7. Be capable of providing informed consent.
8. Have appropriate home support to facilitate virtual ward care

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Experience recurrent angina or ischemia on minimal exertion.
2. Require ongoing intravenous therapies.
3. Possess severe comorbidities necessitating inpatient management.
4. Exhibit cognitive impairment or demonstrate unreliability in self-care capabilities.
5. Are at high risk of rapid deterioration, such as those with left main stenosis exhibiting unstable features.
6. Have sustained ventricular arrhythmias.
7. Present with critical aortic stenosis.
8. Have critical left main coronary artery stenosis.
